description: Coding agents' CLIs in their own terminal UIs inside the window, with an MCP server through which agents start, list and end each other, and message each other and the person.
config.title: Facade Agents
config.enabled: Let Facade run coding agents - Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Muse Code - each in its own terminal. Start one from the Command Palette with **Facade: Start Agent**; agents can start more. When this is off, Facade starts nothing.
config.timeout: How many seconds Facade waits before it gives up: for a new agent to start - one that has not started by then is stopped - and, after this window reloads, for the agents still running to reach it again. It is also how long an agent's task, or a message to it, may wait unfetched before Facade tells the one who sent it.
config.launch.arguments: Command-line arguments, group by group, in this order: `warmUp`, `connect`, `quiet`, `questions` (what takes away its tools for asking with buttons, which wait in its terminal for someone to click), `messages` (what lets it read, without asking, the files Facade writes for it: those of long messages, in `${messagesDir}`, and of screens, in `${screensDir}`), `fullAccess`, `model`, `effort`, `extra` (for your own), `task` (the agent's first line, which names its task). A group you set replaces Facade's; `null` leaves it out. Facade fills in `${model}`, `${effort}`, `${task}` and the like for each agent.
config.launch.environment: Environment variables Facade sets for each agent. One you set replaces Facade's; `null` removes one of Facade's.
config.launch.trust: What Facade does in a worktree it made, so that the CLI does not stop to ask whether you trust the folder: `arguments` given that run, or `merge` written into the CLI's own `file`. `null`: Facade does nothing, and the CLI asks in its terminal.
config.launch.enterDelay: Milliseconds between typing a line into the agent's terminal and pressing Enter: the CLI may take fast typing for a paste.
config.launch.taskDelay: Milliseconds to wait, once the agent is up, before typing anything into its terminal: its first line, for CLIs that get it that way, or the line that tells it of unread messages.
config.claude.launch.settings: Claude Code settings for each agent, on top of yours, key by key; `null` removes one of Facade's. One value of a kind Claude Code does not take makes it ignore all of them.
config.claude.title: Claude Code
config.claude.path: The Claude Code program to run. Leave it empty to use `claude` from your PATH.
config.claude.launch: How Facade starts Claude Code. Write only what you change: in settings.json, choose a part inside the braces to fill in Facade's own, then change it; `null` removes one of Facade's. **Facade: Show Agent Launch** shows what each CLI is started with now.
